events.title: The papacy returns to Rome
events.shortBlurb: Pope Gregory XI re-entered Rome, ending nearly seventy years of the popes' residence at Avignon…
body: On 17 January 1377 Pope Gregory XI entered Rome, ending the residence of the popes at Avignon that had lasted since 1309. He had left that city the previous September, deaf to the pleas of the French court, and sailed from Marseille by way of Genoa for Italy.

The return had long been urged as a matter of conscience. Bridget of Sweden had warned earlier popes from Rome, and Catherine of Siena had journeyed to Avignon in 1376 to press Gregory in person, bidding him manfully fulfill the vow he had secretly made to restore the see to its own city.

The homecoming proved fragile, for Rome had suffered in the popes' absence and their court had grown French. Gregory died on 27 March 1378, and the disputed election of Urban VI that followed opened the Great Western Schism, in which rival popes at Rome and Avignon divided Christendom for nearly forty years.
